text.en: NUMERICAL METHODS ATLAS · PROBLEM Periodic-He₂ forces: analytic derivatives, finite differences and BOMD interface Explore this problem’s equations, reference conditions, methods and published code. Saved result figure Asymmetric-He₂ analytic forces versus energy finite differences and DFTK reference. Force k-point, basis, FFT and SCF refinement, plus a local BOMD interface check. Equations and problem definitions Representative equations related to this problem. See the image/problem conditions and each execution example for initial conditions, boundary conditions and parameters. Local Kohn–Sham DFT E[n]=Ts[n]+∫vextn dr+EH[n]+Exc[n]+ENN [−12∇2+vext+vH+vxc]ϕi=εiϕi n(r)=∑ifi∣ϕi(r)∣2,∫n dr=N,vxc=δExcδn Representative local Kohn–Sham equations. Published examples cover spin-unpolarized exchange-only Dirac LDA for spherical helium and LDA exchange plus VWN5 correlation for fixed periodic He/He₂ cells. The radial atomic implementation and periodic PySCF workflows are separate series with different bases, boundaries and references. Inspect each input and validation record below; these examples do not validate GGA, hybrids, general materials or excited states. Formulations used by execution examples Common execution exampleDiagnostic definition Periodic-He₂ forces: analytic derivatives, finite differences and BOMD interface FIα=−∂EBO∂RIα FIαFD(h)=−E(R+heIα)−E(R−heIα)2h Asymmetric two-He periodic cell with local GTH and LDA exchange plus VWN5. Compare PySCF analytic forces, including Gaussian-basis derivatives, with energy finite differences for all six coordinates and independent DFTK plane waves. Separate force basis, k-point, SCF and FFT refinement. BOMD coverage is a force interface and short step comparison; long NVE, CPMD and general materials remain unvalidated. Exact and reference solutions Distinguish energy finite differences versus analytic forces, independent DFTK references and stored convergence checks for fixed He₂ configurations. This certifies no long-time first-principles MD accuracy. References and results of execution examples Common execution example Periodic-He₂ forces: analytic derivatives, finite differences and BOMD interface Independent DFTK plane waves: Gamma/2³ analytic forces, eight cutoff settings and all-six-coordinate energy finite differences. State shared Libxc formulas and different finite-basis limits. Independent DFTK plane waves: Gamma/2³ analytic forces, eight cutoff settings and all-six-coordinate energy finite differences. State shared Libxc formulas and different finite-basis limits. Compare PySCF analytic forces, including Gaussian-basis derivatives, with energy finite differences for all six coordinates and independent DFTK plane waves. Separate force basis, k-point, SCF and FFT refinement. BOMD coverage is a force interface and short step comparison; long NVE, CPMD and general materials remain unvalidated. Conditions, commands and validation scope Assumptions Fixed asymmetric two-He cell (5-bohr cubic lattice, four valence electrons, unpolarized integer occupations, local GTH and LDA_X plus VWN5). A library-backed PySCF validation driver; not physical equilibrium helium or long-time MD. Use these commands in the working directory specified by the execution guide after extracting the ZIP. A command may execute several cases in the package. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python run.py --input inputs.json --output output python -m pytest -q test_periodic_forces.py Validation limits Reject invalid models, nonfinite values, altered references, SCF nonconvergence and missed force/refinement criteria. Do not pass unconverged forces to BOMD. A short step comparison does not establish long-time NVE conservation.
